records.text: Then Eliphaz the Temanite replied:
“Have you not often been spoken to amid trouble? Who will endure the force of your words?
For if you admonished many and encouraged a weak person’s hands,
and raised up the weak with words and put courage into powerless knees,
yet now pain has come upon you and touched you, and you have become agitated.
Is not your fear in foolishness, and your hope and the innocence of your way as well?
Remember, then: who perished while pure, or when were true people utterly uprooted?
As I have seen those who plow improper things, those who sow them will reap pains for themselves.
The lion’s strength, the lioness’s voice, and the boasting of dragons were extinguished.
The ant-lion perished for lack of food, and lion cubs abandoned one another.
But if some true word had been among your words, none of these evils would have met you. Will not my ear receive extraordinary things from Him?
There were terrors and a nocturnal sound, fear falling upon people;
a shudder and trembling met me and shook my bones greatly.
A spirit came upon my face, and my hair and flesh shuddered.
‘What then? Can a mortal be pure before the Lord, or a man blameless on account of his works?
“Call, then, to see whether anyone will answer you, or whether you will see any of the holy angels.
For anger kills a fool, and jealousy puts one who has gone astray to death.
I have seen fools taking root, but immediately their way of life was devoured.
May their sons be far from deliverance; may they be battered at the doors of weaker people, with no one to rescue them.
For toil will certainly not come out of the earth, nor will pain sprout from mountains;
but a human being is born to toil, and a vulture’s young fly to the heights.
But indeed, I will entreat the Lord; I will call upon the Lord, the Master of all,
Now we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to Him,
not to be quickly shaken from your understanding or alarmed, either by a spirit or by a word or by a letter as though from us, as if the day of the Lord is already present.
Let no one deceive you in any way. For that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of destruction,
who opposes and exalts himself above everything called god or an object of worship, so that he takes his seat in God’s sanctuary, displaying himself as being God.
Do you not remember that when I was still with you I used to tell you these things?
And now you know what restrains, so that he may be revealed in his own time.
For the mystery of lawlessness is already at work. Only, the one who now restrains does so until he is out of the way.
His coming is according to the working of Satan, with all power and signs and wonders of falsehood,
and with every deception of unrighteousness for those who are perishing, because they did not receive the love of the truth so that they might be saved.
And for this reason God sends them a working of delusion, so that they believe the falsehood,
in order that all who did not believe the truth but took pleasure in unrighteousness may be judged.

Take heed unto yourself, and guard your soul diligently, lest you forget all the things which your eyes have seen, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life. And you shall teach your sons and your sons’ sons

the day when you stood before the Lord your God in Horeb, in the day of the assembly, when the Lord said unto me: Assemble the people unto Me, and let them hear My words, that they may learn to fear Me all the days that they live upon the earth, and may teach their sons.
And you drew near and stood beneath the mountain; and the mountain burned with fire unto heaven, with darkness, gloom, tempest, and a great sound.
And He declared unto you His covenant, which He commanded you to do, even the ten words; and He wrote them upon two tablets of stone.
And the Lord commanded me at that time to teach you ordinances and judgments, that you should do them in the land whither you go to inherit it.
And you shall guard your souls diligently; for you saw no likeness in the day when the Lord spoke unto you in Horeb, on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire,
lest you act lawlessly and make for yourselves a graven likeness, any image, the likeness of male or female,
One who walks with the wise will be wise, but one who walks with fools will be known.
Evils will pursue those who sin, but good things will overtake the righteous.
The righteous will spend many years in wealth, but the unjust will perish swiftly.
One who spares the staff hates his son, but one who loves him disciplines carefully.
The righteous, by eating, fills his life, but the lives of the impious are in want.
Then Job replied:
“If only someone would weigh my anger and lift my pains together in a balance!
It would indeed be heavier than the sand beside the sea; but, it seems, my words are worthless.
For the Lord’s arrows are in my body; their fury drinks up my blood. When I begin to speak, they stab me.
What then? Does a wild donkey cry out for nothing, rather than seeking food? Would an ox raise its voice at a manger when it has food?
Will bread be eaten without salt? Is there any taste in empty words?
For my soul cannot cease; I see my food as a stench, like the smell of a lion.
If only He would grant it and my request would come, and the Lord would grant my hope!
Let the Lord begin and wound me, but let Him not destroy me completely.
May my city be a grave, on whose walls I used to leap; I will certainly not hold back. For I have not falsified the holy words of my God.
For what is my strength, that I endure? What time remains to me, that my soul holds out?
Is my strength the strength of stones? Is my flesh made of bronze?
Mercy has disowned me, and the Lord’s care has overlooked me.
For what is a human being, that Thou didst magnify him, or that Thou givest Thy mind to him,
or that Thou visitest him until morning and judgest him for rest?
How long wilt Thou not leave me alone, nor let me go until I swallow my saliva in pain?
If I sinned, what can I do to Thee, Thou who understandest the human mind? Why hast Thou made me Thine accuser, and why am I a burden to Thee?
For the end, concerning the help of the morning. A psalm of David.
God, my God, attend to me; why didst Thou abandon me? Far from my salvation are the words of my transgressions.
My God, I will cry by day, and Thou wilt not hear, and by night, and not to folly for me.
But Thou dwellest among holy ones, the praise of Israel.
In Thee our fathers hoped; they hoped, and Thou didst rescue them.
To Thee they cried out and were saved; in Thee they hoped and were not put to shame.
Rescue my soul from the sword and my only one from the dog’s hand.
Save me from a lion’s mouth and my lowliness from the horns of one-horned animals.
I will recount Thy name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will sing hymns unto Thee:
You who fear the Lord, praise Him! All Jacob’s seed, glorify Him! Let all Israel’s seed fear Him,
because He did not despise or resent the poor man’s petition, nor turn His face away from me, and when I cried out to Him, He heard me.
Rescue me from all my lawless deeds; Thou hast given me as a reproach to a fool.
I became mute and did not open my mouth, because Thou art the One who made me.
Remove Thy scourges from me; from the strength of Thy hand I wasted away.
With rebukes for lawlessness Thou didst discipline a person and melt his soul like a spider. Yet every person is troubled in vain. Diapsalma.
Then Job replied:
“Truly I know that it is so; for how can a mortal be righteous before the Lord?
For if he wishes to enter judgment with Him, He certainly will not listen to him, lest he answer back to one of His words out of a thousand.
He wears the mountains out, and they do not know; He overturns them in anger.
He shakes the world beneath heaven from its foundations, and its pillars sway.
He speaks to the sun and it does not rise, and He seals up the stars.
He alone stretched out heaven and walks on the sea as on ground.
He makes the Pleiades, the Evening Star, and Arcturus, and the storehouses of the south.
He does great and unsearchable things, glorious and extraordinary things beyond numbering.
What, then, shall we say? Is there unrighteousness with God? May it never be!
For He says to Moses, “I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.”
So then, it depends not on the one who wills, nor on the one who runs, but on God who has mercy.
For the Scripture says to Pharaoh, “For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might demonstrate My power in you, and so that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth.”
So then, He has mercy on whom He wills, and whom He wills He hardens.
Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, from the same lump to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?
Why, then, didst Thou bring me out of the womb? Why did I not die with no eye seeing me,
and become as though I had not existed? For why was I not taken from the womb to the tomb?
Is not the time of my life short? Let me rest a little
before I go where I will not return, to a dark and gloomy land,
A song of a psalm for the sons of Korah. For the end; concerning Maeleth, for answering. Of understanding; of Heman the Israelite.
Lord, God of my salvation, by day I cried out, and by night before Thee.
Let my prayer enter before Thee; incline Thine ear to my petition, Lord.
For my soul was filled with evils, and my life drew near Hades.
I was counted with those descending into a pit; I became like a person without help, free among the dead,
like wounded people cast down, sleeping in a grave, whom Thou didst remember no more, and who were thrust away from Thy hand.
They put me in the lowest pit, in dark places and in death’s shadow.
Thy fury rested firmly upon me, and Thou broughtest all Thy surges upon me. Diapsalma.
Thou didst remove my acquaintances far from me; they made me an abomination to themselves. I was handed over and did not go out.
My eyes grew weak from poverty. I cried unto Thee, Lord, all day; I spread my hands toward Thee:
Surely Thou wilt not work wonders for the dead? Or will physicians raise them, and will they give Thee thanks?
And I cried unto Thee, Lord, and in the morning my prayer will reach Thee first.
Why, Lord, dost Thou thrust away my soul and turn Thy face away from me?
I am poor and in toils from my youth; but after being raised up, I was humbled and left helpless.
